local_patches.why: back the CUDA caching allocator with expandable (VMM) segments, set before CUDA is initialized and again in Worker.init_device; only the mapping under an allocator segment changes (VLLM_EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=0 keeps the default allocator)
GB10 exposes no NVML memory clock; fall back to 273 GB/s for humming's tuning heuristic
VLLM_HUMMING_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 turns on humming's deterministic MoE kernels without the global batch-invariant mode (which forces CUTLASS W4A4 on W4A16 linears)

when the optional l2pf kernel package (harness/kernels/l2pf) is importable, the FULL CUDA graph gets one extra side-stream node per GEMM that L2-prefetches the first tiles of the next GEMM's weights; the GEMM sites are recorded on the warm-up run before the capture, only model parameters are prefetched, and no kernel on the main stream changes (L2PF=0 turns it off)

the accepted glimmer_fp8_ext G2 tile serves the supported small FP8 GEMMs on GB10 with the stock accumulation order and scale rounding. L2 prefetch records the actual native launch or the stock CUTLASS overload with the same model weight pointer

local_patches.file: vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/ssd_pinned_configs.py (+ pins in ssd_state_passing.py, ssd_bmm.py, ssd_chunk_scan.py, ssd_chunk_state.py)
local_patches.why: Triton autotune picked different SSD tile configs per boot on GB10, making the same prompt yield one of two token streams; each kernel is pinned to one config (VLLM_MAMBA_SSD_AUTOTUNE=1 restores autotuning)

the attention output gate projection reads the layer input, so for decode-sized batches it is launched before attention and the attention chain (QK-norm, RoPE, KV-cache write, attention) runs beside it on a high-priority side stream; fork, switch and join are graph splitting points, so the gate projection is a compiled piece of its own and the FULL CUDA graph gets a fork and a join; the same kernels run on the same inputs, unquantized (cuBLAS) gate projections keep the stock order (VLLM_MUSE_GLIMMER_GATE_STREAM=0 turns it off)
skip the MTP drafter when every request in the batch has max_tokens == 1: its drafts are never verified, and the drafter's pass over the prompt delayed the sampled token (the timed prefill)

NVFP4 W4A16 weights much larger than L2 (MLP gate_up and down) run calls of 128 rows or more through harness/kernels/marlinw when it is built (the Marlin kernel body on the same work slices as ops.marlin_gemm, handed out column-major); a layer without it runs prompt-sized calls as ops.marlin_gemm on column slices of a slice-major copy of the same prepared weight where both schedules compute every tile whole-K with the same config, else the single call; each path is admitted per layer by a load-time bitwise comparison with the single call

in-process engine core for the single-request engine loop: InprocClient pauses automatic garbage collection while the engine has work and drains a finished request's queued batch on abort (no busy loop does it in this mode); hostfast.py also restricts the process to the highest-capacity CPU cores when the cores differ, failing soft (VLLM_HOSTFAST_GC=0 and VLLM_HOSTFAST_PIN=0 switch each off)

one-token FP8 w8a8 GEMMs (decode) run through musefp8, a hand-written mma.sync m16n8k32 e4m3 GEMV that issues the same instruction chain in the same k order as cutlass_scaled_mm's SM120 M16 kernel and the same ScaledEpilogue (bf16_rn(scale_a * fp32(scale_b * acc))), reading a fragment-ordered copy of each weight (registered as a layer buffer) with L2 evict-first loads; every layer is admitted only after a load-time bitwise comparison with cutlass_scaled_mm; other row counts keep glimmer_fp8 / cutlass; the op is an l2pf site (MUSEFP8=0 disables, MUSEFP8_L2PF=0 drops it from the prefetch chain). When harness/kernels/muserans is built, each FP8 weight is instead stored as an exponent-pair rANS stream with raw sign|mantissa nibbles (lossless, ~0.84 of the bytes on this checkpoint) and decoded inside the same GEMV right before the same mma.sync chain, so the output bits are unchanged and the decode step reads fewer bytes; admitted per layer by the same bitwise check (MUSERANS=0 keeps the uncompressed copy).

One-row NVFP4 decode (decode6) packs each layer's 64 unique E4M3 group scales into 6-bit palette codes and pre-dequantizes the 64-entry palette directly into BF16 shared memory (sh_pal16[64]), eliminating per-step FP8-to-BF16 register conversion, with adaptive SM120/SM121 tile-N dispatch, in-place lm_head tiling, 10-bit rANS entropy-coded gate/up block scales (gemv6_srans.cu on 48-SM SM121, MUSE_SCALE_RANS, MUSE_GATE_UP_SRANS=0 disables), and redundant 8-bit scale release after per-layer bitwise admission checks.

The single-device 512-row static FP8 MLP gate/up dispatches to harness/kernels/muse_fp8_swiglu when its down projection accepts static FP8. Alternating checkpoint output columns brings the BF16 gate and up values into one CUTLASS thread fragment. The arithmetic uses the G2 scaled-MM multiply order and the existing BF16 SiLU lookup before packing the down-scale E4M3 byte. The input uses its original FP8 quantizer before shape dispatch.

Prompt-batch query QK-norm and RoPE Triton launcher hook replacing the symbolic-stride compiled pointwise kernel on batches >= 128 tokens after bitwise verification against the stock compiled kernel on live and synthetic inputs.

The unquantized BF16 Muse Glimmer QKV and output gate on one CUDA device admit the one-row lane-striped GEMV only after a complete lossless weight check and per-layer bitwise cuBLAS comparisons. It keeps the original lane accumulation and warp fold. Larger row counts, bias and other weights retain the stock linear method. The original weights remain the fallback and the L2 site reads only the registered compact buffer. MUSE_BF16_LANE=0 selects the original paths.

Keep the full compiled backbone and specialize only the final two independent-row NVFP4 projection launches inside the logits-only prefill capture (using muse_final_slab narrow tiles on SM121 and marlinw.gemm_last_chunk on SM120, plus routing final_slab_shape through marlin_fp4_single_or_tiled). Retain both operator output shapes and the ordered K partition for the sampled tile. Full-output consumers use the original projection launches.

The 512-row NVFP4 attention projections (qkv 4608x6656, output gate 4096x6656, o 6656x4096) on 48-SM SM121 run the stock ops.marlin_gemm partition on the narrow marlinw_down kernel (two blocks per SM, one block per 128-column half of each stock slice, unsplit tiles column-major, cut slices longest first). Every slice keeps its chunk, K range, slice_idx and slice_count, so each output element keeps its K16 MMA chains, FP32 split-K order and BF16 epilogue. Admitted only after a bitwise comparison with the single ops.marlin_gemm call; MARLIN_NARROW_ATTN=0 disables it.

On a 128 GB unified-memory GB10 GPU (SM121), NVFP4 decode GEMV and 512-row prefill MLP bandwidth vary across physical allocations. After model load on SM121, same-shaped decode and 512-row prefill weights above 48 MiB are timed on their home buffers and spare buffers; slower weights are copied to faster spares and verified bit-for-bit before swapping (skipped on discrete-VRAM SM120; MUSE_DECODE_PLACEMENT=0 / MUSE_PREFILL_PLACEMENT=0 disable).
512-row prefill FP8 scaled-MM kernels (fp8ws) and final lm_head softcap+argmax fusion (lmpost) with bitwise load-time checks against stock CUTLASS and logits processor.

Native CUDA sandwich normalization kernels matching compiled Inductor reductions; admitted per kernel object and row count at first eager launch after bitwise verification across all output buffers against the compiled Triton kernel.

local_patches.file: harness/vllm_resident/settle.py (new), harness/vllm_resident/resident.py (outside the vLLM subtree; recorded here for provenance)
local_patches.why: After model load and warm-up, trim freed Python heap pages back to the kernel and wait until Linux /proc/vmstat compaction/reclaim counters and background CPU usage settle before reporting ready on the resident socket (RESIDENT_SETTLE=0 skips).

Full load-time/first-use lossless weight checks and bitwise output verifications across muserans/musefp8, decode6 (including fixed-grid gate_up), muse_fp8_swiglu, sandwich, muse_final_slab, and l2pf recursion guard recording each wrapped GEMM site once at the outermost call.

Non-blocking CUDA event + spin-wait synchronization between single-request decode steps (VLLM_SPIN_OUTPUT_WAIT=0 disables), cached single-request metadata tensors skipping redundant per-step H2D copies, and skipping the redundant 8192-token FlashInfer dummy autotune pass when 0 ops are tuned.
